runs.prompt:
Use your built-in image generation tool to create ONE raster image and save it as island-map.png in the current directory. Do not draw it with code, SVG or a plotting library; if you have no image generation tool, say so plainly and stop.

The image: an original bird's-eye fold-out souvenir map of one tiny tropical desert island, seen from above at a slight three-quarter angle. It is printed on worn cream paper that has been folded into a 4 by 2 grid and unfolded many times: soft crease lines, slightly frayed edges, a few faint stains.

The island: a small oval sandbank with one leaning coconut palm a little right of centre, a small wooden raft pulled up on the east shore, a grey rock in the shallows to the west, and a pale ring of shallow water. Deep blue sea fills most of the map, with a few simple hand-inked wave marks.

Leave the sea and the sand mostly EMPTY: no people, no creatures, no boats, no text, no labels, no lettering, no compass rose. Painted objects will be placed on top later, so there must be clear open water on every side of the island and open sand on it.

Style: hand-painted gouache with deep palm-green ink contours; sun-bleached driftwood, cream and faded aqua palette with small orange highlights; warm, sunny, 1992 illustrated adventure-game box art; chunky, friendly, substantial shapes. Not photorealistic, not a 3D render, not pixel art. Match the painting style and palette of the reference image style-reference.png in this directory. Landscape, about 3:2, at least 1536 pixels wide.

When done, reply with the file name and its pixel size.

processing: Each object was cut from its sheet by connected alpha region (so no neighbour's edge is included), cropped, scaled to fit 300x300 and saved as lossy WebP quality 90 with alpha. The base was saved as WebP quality 86. No repainting or colour changes.
originals: The full-resolution PNG sheets and base are not in the repository; they are linked from issue #96.
concept: The beach layout follows concept art generated with Antigravity (agy 1.5.3) on 2026-11-13 from four briefed directions; the owner chose 'On the beach'. The concept image itself is not an asset and is not in the repository.
